II.}}}}</noinclude>Spirit {{ls}}earcheth al things, yea the profoundities of God. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=11|align=float}}† For vvhat man knovveth the things of a man, but {{sup|‖}} the {{ls}}pirit of a man that is in him? {{ls}}o the things al{{ls}}o that are of God no man knovveth, but the {{ls}}pirit of God.

{{verse|chapter=2|verse=12|align=float}}† And vve haue receiued not the {{ls}}pirit of this vvorld, but the {{ls}}pirit that is of God: {{sup|‖}} that vve may knovv the things that of God are giuen to vs. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=13|align=float}}† vvhich al{{ls}}o vve {{ls}}peake not in learned vvordes of humane vvi{{ls}}edom: but in the doctrine of the Spirit, comparing {{ls}}piritual things to the {{ls}}piritual. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=14|align=float}}† But {{sup|‖}} the {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual man perceiueth not tho{{ls}}e things that are of the {{ls}}pirit of God. for it is foli{{ls}}hnes to him, and he can not vnder{{ls}}tand: becau{{ls}}e he is {{ls}}piritually examined. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=15|align=float}}† But the {{ls}}piritual man iudgeth al things: and him {{ls}}elf is iudged of no man. {{verse|chapter=2|verse=16|align=float}}† For * {{outside R|''E{{ls}}a. 40, 13.''}} vvho hath knovven the {{ls}}en{{ls}}e of our Lord that may in{{ls}}tructe him? Reg. 5. & 6.''}}to knovv the fraude of Ananias and Saphira: and to Eli{{ls}}eus, his {{ls}}eruants bribery in his ab{{ls}}ence, and vvhat was done in the king of Syria his chamber. and as he giueth to al {{outside R|''* Luc. 15, 7.''}}Angels and Saincts ({{ls}}o far as is conuenient for our nece{{ls}}sities and their heauenly glorie) to vnder{{ls}}tand not onely our vocal praiers, but our invvard repentance and de{{ls}}ires.

That we may knovv.''] {{outside L|The Heretikes allegation for their vaine {{ls}}ecuritie, an{{ls}}wered.}}The Prote{{ls}}tants that chalenge a particular {{ls}}pirit reuealing to eche one his ovvne prede{{ls}}tination, iu{{ls}}tification, and {{ls}}aluation, would dravv this text to that purpo{{ls}}e. Vvhich importeth nothing els (as is plaine by the Apo{{ls}}tles di{{ls}}cour{{ls}}e) but that the holy Gho{{ls}}t hath giuen to the Apo{{ls}}tles, & by them to other Chri{{ls}}tian men, to knovv Gods ineffable gifts be{{ls}}tovved vpon the beleeuers in this time of grace: that is, Chri{{ls}}tes Incarnation, Pa{{ls}}sion, pre{{ls}}ence in the Sacrament, & the incomprehen{{ls}}ible ioyes of heauen, which Pagans, Ievves, and Heretikes deride.

The {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual man.''] {{outside L|The {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual man.}}The {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual man is he {{ls}}pecially, that mea{{ls}}ureth the{{ls}}e heauenly my{{ls}}teries by natural rea{{ls}}on, humane prudence, external {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, and worldly affection, as the Ievv, Pagane, and Heretike doe: and {{ls}}ometime both here and els vvhere, the more infirme and ignorant {{ls}}ort of Chri{{ls}}tian men be called {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual or carnal al{{ls}}o, vvho being occupied in {{ls}}ecular affaires, and giuen to {{ls}}en{{ls}}ual ioy and worldlines, haue no {{ls}}uch {{ls}}en{{ls}}e nor feeling of the{{ls}}e great gifts of God, as the perfecter {{ls}}ort of the faithful haue. Who trying the{{ls}}e high pointes of religion, not by rea{{ls}}on and {{ls}}en{{ls}}e, but by grace, faith, and Spirit, be therfore called {{ls}}piritual. {{outside L|The {{ls}}piritual man.}}The {{ls}}piritual then is he, that iudgeth and di{{ls}}cerneth the truth of {{ls}}uch things as the carnal can not attaine vnto: that doth by the {{ls}}pirit of the Church, vvhereof he is partaker in the vnitie of the {{ls}}ame, not onely {{ls}}ee the errours of the carnal, but condemneth them and iudgeth euery povver re{{ls}}i{{ls}}ting Gods {{ls}}pirit and word: the carnal Ievv, Heathen, or Heretike, hauing no meanes nor right to iudge of the {{ls}}aid {{ls}}piritual man. {{outside L|How the {{ls}}piritual man iudgeth al, & is iudged of none.}}For when the {{ls}}piritual is {{ls}}aid to be iudged of none, the meaning is not that he {{ls}}hould not be {{ls}}ubiect or obedient to his Pa{{ls}}tors and {{ls}}piritual Povvers and to the vvhole Church, {{ls}}pecially for the trial or examination of al his life, doctrine, and faith: but that a Catholike man and namely a teacher of Catholike doctrine in the Church, {{ls}}hould not be any vvhit {{ls}}ubiect to the iudgement of the Heathen or the Heretike, nor care what of ignorance or infidelitie they {{ls}}ay again{{ls}}t him. for {{ls}}uch carnal men haue no iudgement in {{ls}}uch things, nor can attaine to the Churches wi{{ls}}edom in any ceremonie, my{{ls}}terie, or matter vvhich they condemne.<noinclude>{{continues|Therfore}}
